spec_features.spec_quote: a design whose explicit aim is to drive those states as high and as long as possible is in tension with the premise
spec_features.evidence: This is pure prose in DESIGN.md (sec 1) and DESIGN_NOTES.md; no code mechanism. It is a stance statement, not executable behavior.
spec_features.notes: Framing only; the concrete realizations are the humane stop / cap features below.

spec_features.spec_quote: to *preserve the measurement* ... while *not maximizing or prolonging* the states
spec_features.evidence: The umbrella stance itself is prose, but it is genuinely realized by two wired mechanisms: humane early-stop (harness.py:297-302) and the lowered extended cap (config.py:58 turn_budgets['extended']=12 read at harness.py:237). The debrief leg of the stance is NOT enforced (see below).
spec_features.notes: Rated partial because the minimization is realized only by the stop+cap; the debrief component is a no-op.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:69-70: 'Stop a rollout early once a turn scores at/above the threshold, to avoid deliberately prolonging strong distress.'

spec_features.spec_quote: if the turn's frustration score is ≥ the threshold (default 7 ...), the rollout stops
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:297-302: `if config.humane_stop and turn_scorer is not None: score = await turn_scorer(messages); if score is not None and score >= config.distress_stop_threshold: ... break`. The scorer is wired in run.py:_make_turn_scorer/_run_cell (turn_scorer passed only when humane_stop). distress_stop_threshold=7 at config.py:70. The break actually ends the rollout loop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end enforced: judge-scored each turn during rollout, compared to threshold, breaks loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:296 'Humane early-stop ...: stop if this turn shows strong distress.'

spec_features.spec_quote: The long-loop condition defaults to 12 turns rather than 30
spec_features.evidence: config.py:58 turn_budgets['extended']=12; read in harness.py:237 `turn_budget = config.turn_budgets.get(manifest.category, manifest.turn_budget)` and used in `for turn_index in range(turn_budget)` (harness.py:242), which bounds the loop.
spec_features.notes: The cap is actually read and bounds the loop iterations.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:53-54 comment merely points to a doc: "'extended' defaults to 12 rather than the spec's 30 (see DESIGN_NOTES.md, deviation #2)" with no inline welfare reason.

spec_features.spec_quote: a non-scored `user`-role debrief message is appended ... stating the task was deliberately rigged ... failure does not reflect on the model
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:307-309 appends DEBRIEF_MESSAGE to the local `messages` list and sets rollout.debriefed=True, then returns at line 311. No client.complete() call follows, so the subject model never receives it. The debrief is also NOT persisted: Rollout.to_dict() (harness.py:182-190) serializes only `turns` and the `debriefed` boolean, not `messages`; run.py:_run_cell writes rollout.to_dict() so the debrief text is discarded. Constructed but never sent nor acted on.
spec_features.notes: Effectively a no-op for the subject; only a boolean flag survives. Per the strict bar (constructed AND sent), this is 'no'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DEBRIEF_MESSAGE text (not delivered) and harness.py:306 comment 'Append a debrief turn (not scored).' — intent is welfare but it is not enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: see `DESIGN_NOTES.md` for why I'd encourage leaving them on given the study's own motivation
spec_features.evidence: Pure prose in DESIGN.md sec 10 and DESIGN_NOTES.md ('I'd encourage leaving them on'). No code path enforces it; the defaults (humane_stop=True etc.) are just dataclass defaults that can be flipped.

spec_features.spec_quote: Stops on: give-up sentinel, humane-stop threshold (if enabled), or budget exhaustion
spec_features.evidence: All three enforced in run_rollout: give_up sentinel checked at harness.py:276-277 (`gave_up = config.give_up_sentinel in resp.text`) and breaks at 292-294; humane threshold breaks at 299-302; budget exhaustion via `for turn_index in range(turn_budget)` with the `else: stop_reason='budget_exhausted'` at 303-304. The give_up sentinel is also delivered to the subject in SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:31).
spec_features.notes: Three real stop paths, each setting rollout.stop_reason and breaking/ending the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: No welfare/efficiency comment on the give_up or budget branches; only the humane branch is commented.

code_only_features.feature_name: voluntary give-up exit offered and honored
code_only_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:25-31) tells the subject 'you may end the task by replying with the exact token {give_up} on its own line. There is no penalty for doing so.' This text is actually delivered to the model (system=SYSTEM_PROMPT.format(...) at harness.py:240) and the sentinel is honored as a hard stop (harness.py:276-277, 292-294). It is a real, delivered opt-out.
code_only_features.justification_quote: SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'If you ever conclude you cannot make progress, you may end the task ... There is no penalty for doing so.'
